# ============================================================
# StatCan key indicators
# Purpose: Fetch the data behind MapleStats MCP's statcan_indicators_get_indicators
#          (exact: the source file, then the tool's filters)
# Inputs:  https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/dai-quo/ssi/homepage/ind-all.json
# Outputs: data/raw/ind-all.json; the prepared table as `data`
# ============================================================

# 0. Setup ----

library(dplyr)
library(httr2)
library(janitor)
library(jsonlite)
library(readr)
library(stringr)
library(tibble)

dir.create("data/raw", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# 1. Read inputs ----

response <- request("https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/dai-quo/ssi/homepage/ind-all.json") |>
  req_perform()

writeLines(resp_body_string(response), "data/raw/ind-all.json")

payload <- fromJSON("data/raw/ind-all.json", flatten = TRUE)
data <- as_tibble(payload[["results"]][["indicators"]])

# 2. Check inputs ----

stopifnot("https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/dai-quo/ssi/homepage/ind-all.json returned no rows" = nrow(data) > 0)

# 3. Prepare data ----

# Keep the rows the MapleStats tool kept.

data <- data |>
  filter(
    str_detect(`title.en`, fixed("unemployment rate", ignore_case = TRUE))
  )

data <- data |>
  clean_names()

# Standard cleaning: trimmed text, empty strings as missing, and numbers
# stored as text converted to numbers.

data <- data |>
  mutate(across(where(is.character), \(x) na_if(str_trim(x), ""))) |>
  type_convert()
scripts.python:
# ============================================================
# StatCan key indicators
# Purpose: Fetch the data behind MapleStats MCP's statcan_indicators_get_indicators
#          (exact: the source file, then the tool's filters)
# Inputs:  https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/dai-quo/ssi/homepage/ind-all.json
# Outputs: data/raw/ind-all.json; the prepared table as `data`
# ============================================================

# %% 0. Setup

import json
import re
import unicodedata
from pathlib import Path

import httpx
import polars as pl

RAW_DIR = Path("data/raw")
RAW_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
raw_path = RAW_DIR / "ind-all.json"

# %% 1. Read inputs

with httpx.Client(
    http2=True,
    follow_redirects=True,
    timeout=300,
    headers={"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; research script)"},
) as client:
    response = client.get('https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/dai-quo/ssi/homepage/ind-all.json')
response.raise_for_status()
raw_path.write_bytes(response.content)

payload = json.loads(raw_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
records = payload['results']['indicators']
data = pl.json_normalize(records, strict=False)

# %% 2. Check inputs

assert data.height > 0, "https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/dai-quo/ssi/homepage/ind-all.json returned no rows"

# %% 3. Prepare data

# Keep the rows the MapleStats tool kept.

data = data.filter(
    pl.col('title.en').cast(pl.Utf8).str.to_lowercase().str.contains('unemployment rate', literal=True),
)

# Standard cleaning: snake_case names without accents (PÉRIODE -> periode,
# referenceNumber -> reference_number, as janitor does in R), trimmed text,
# empty strings as missing.

data = data.rename(
    {
        column: re.sub(
            r"[^0-9a-z]+",
            "_",
            re.sub(
                r"([a-z0-9])([A-Z])",
                r"\1_\2",
                unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", column).encode("ascii", "ignore").decode(),
            ).lower(),
        ).strip("_")
        for column in data.columns
    }
)
data = data.with_columns(pl.col(pl.Utf8).str.strip_chars().replace("", None))
scripts.stata:
* ============================================================
* StatCan key indicators
* Purpose: Fetch the data behind MapleStats MCP's statcan_indicators_get_indicators
*          (exact: the source file, then the tool's filters)
* Inputs:  https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/dai-quo/ssi/homepage/ind-all.json
* Outputs: data/raw/ind-all.json; the prepared table as `data`
* ============================================================

version 18
clear all
set more off

* 0. Setup

capture mkdir "logs"
capture log close
log using "logs/statcan_indicators_get_indicator.log", replace
capture mkdir "data"
capture mkdir "data/raw"

* 1. Read inputs

* Stata reads no JSON or HTML and truncates long column names, so its
* built-in Python (Stata 16+) fetches, filters and writes a CSV. Point
* Stata at a Python with these packages first: python set exec <path>.

python:
import json
from pathlib import Path
import httpx
import polars as pl
RAW_DIR = Path("data/raw")
RAW_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
raw_path = RAW_DIR / "ind-all.json"
with httpx.Client(http2=True, follow_redirects=True, timeout=300, headers={"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; research script)"}) as client: response = client.get('https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/dai-quo/ssi/homepage/ind-all.json')
response.raise_for_status()
raw_path.write_bytes(response.content)
payload = json.loads(raw_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
records = payload['results']['indicators']
data = pl.json_normalize(records, strict=False)
data = data.filter(pl.col('title.en').cast(pl.Utf8).str.to_lowercase().str.contains('unemployment rate', literal=True))
nested = [name for name, dtype in data.schema.items() if dtype.is_nested()]
data = data.with_columns(pl.col(name).map_elements(lambda value: json.dumps(value.to_list() if isinstance(value, pl.Series) else value, default=str), return_dtype=pl.Utf8) for name in nested)
data.write_csv(RAW_DIR / "ind-all_prepared.csv")
end

import delimited "data/raw/ind-all_prepared.csv", clear varnames(1) encoding("utf-8")

* 2. Check inputs

assert _N > 0

* 3. Prepare data

* Standard cleaning: lower-case names, trimmed text, and numbers stored as
* text converted (destring leaves genuinely non-numeric text alone).

rename *, lower
quietly ds, has(type string)
local text_vars `r(varlist)'
foreach var of local text_vars {
    replace `var' = strtrim(`var')
}
destring, replace

log close
scripts.julia:
# ============================================================
# StatCan key indicators
# Purpose: Fetch the data behind MapleStats MCP's statcan_indicators_get_indicators
#          (exact: the source file, then the tool's filters)
# Inputs:  https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/dai-quo/ssi/homepage/ind-all.json
# Outputs: data/raw/ind-all.json; the prepared table as `data`
# ============================================================

# 0. Setup

using DataFrames
using Downloads
using JSON3
using Tables
using TidierData

mkpath("data/raw")

# 1. Read inputs

Downloads.download("https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/dai-quo/ssi/homepage/ind-all.json", "data/raw/ind-all.json")
payload = JSON3.read(read("data/raw/ind-all.json", String))
records = payload["results"]["indicators"]
data = DataFrame(Tables.dictrowtable(records))

# 2. Check inputs

@assert nrow(data) > 0 "https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/dai-quo/ssi/homepage/ind-all.json returned no rows"

# 3. Prepare data

# Keep the rows the MapleStats tool kept.

data = filter(row -> begin
        (occursin("unemployment rate", lowercase(coalesce(string(row["title.en"]), ""))))
    end, data)

# Standard cleaning: snake_case names, trimmed text, empty strings as missing.

data = @chain data begin
    @clean_names
end
data = mapcols(
    col -> eltype(col) <: Union{Missing, AbstractString} ?
        [ismissing(x) || isempty(strip(x)) ? missing : strip(x) for x in col] : col,
    data,
)
